sentences.text:
Present petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
named above humbly pray that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to pass an Order,
directing the I.O. to release the Petitioner Nos.1 to 6 on anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.0002/2023 of Makikeri Rural PS, registered for the alleged o/p/u/s. 454 and 380 of IPC 1860, pending on the file of the Ld. Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC, Madikeri and grant such other reliefs as the Hon'ble Court deems fit to grant in the facts and circumstances of the case to meet the ends of justice."
3. The brief facts of the case are as under:

A complaint came to be lodged by Hanif M.H. S/o. Late Hamsa with Madikeri Rural Police Station, which was registered in Crime No.2/2023 on 03.01.2023 for the offences punishable under sections 380 and 454 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860(hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short).

The petitioners are the wife,
father-in-law, mother-in-law and relatives of the complainant.

4. The gist of the complaint averments reveals that when the complainant was away from the house,
the petitioners have lurked into the house and thieved the valuables including the bank cheque book and other documents.
Police after registering the case, are investigating the matter.

5. In the meantime, the petitioners have approached the I Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Kodagu at Madikeri for grant of anticipatory bail in Crl. Misc. No.23/2023, which was turned down by order dated 03.02.2023.

entities.text:
I Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Kodagu at Madikeri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioners are before this Court.

6. Reiterating the grounds urged in the bail petition Miss. Keerthana Nagaraj, learned counsel for the petitioners vehemently contended that as a counter blast to the case filed by the petitioners, for the harassment meted out to the petitioner No.1 by the complainant, the present case came to be filed on fictitious and imaginary grounds and therefore, sought for grant of anticipatory bail.
7. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader however opposes for grant of anticipatory bail by filing detailed written objections.
8. In the light of the rival contentions, this Court perused the materials on record meticulously.
9. On such perusal of the materials on record, it is seen that there is a delay of 17 days in filing the complaint.

10. Admittedly, a complaint came to be filed by the petitioner No.1 against the complainant, which is now pending for adjudication in Crime No.156/2022 of Madikeri Rural Police for the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC.
11.
Therefore, there is sufficient force in the arguments putforth on behalf of the petitioners that the present complaint came to be filed as a counter blast.

sentences.text:
Anyway, it is for the Investigating Agency to investigate the matter and arrive at a proper conclusion and file appropriate report as is contemplated under Section 173 of Cr.P.C.
13.

Suffice to say that from the date of registration of the case, the petitioners are not available to the Investigation Agency and therefore, investigation has crippled.
14.
Directing the petitioners to join the investigation and undergo limited period of custodial investigation would meet the ends of justice.
15. Accordingly, without expressing further opinion on merits of the matter, the following order is passed.
ORDER 1. The Criminal Petition is allowed.

2. Petitioners are directed to appear before the Investigating Agency on 30.03.2023 at about 10.00 a.m.
3.

Investigation Officer is at liberty to take the accused / petitioners to custody and complete the custodial investigation on the same day, before 5.00 p.m. and thereafter, enlarge the petitioners on bail, on each of the petitioners executing a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only)
with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
4. Petitioners shall co

-operate with the Investigating Agency and in that regard directed that petitioners shall mark their attendance before the Investigating Officer on every alternate Sunday between 10.00 am and 2.00 pm., till the final report is filed.
5. Petitioners shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
6. Petitioners shall attend the Court regularly.
If any of the above conditions are violated, the prosecution is at liberty to seek cancellation of this bail order.
Ordered accordingly.
